paragraphs: Children in care in the Wakefield district are looked after by the council's own service, Fostering Wakefield, and by the independent agencies listed on this page. In January 2025 the council said 680 local children were in care, and that some had to be placed outside the district because there were not enough local foster carers. Fostering is open to single people, couples and people who already have children, and the council says you do not need to be a parent, own your home or have experience.

Teenagers are the clearest local need. In October 2025 the council said teenagers make up more than 40% of the children it looks after, and that 126 of them were living outside the district, away from their schools and support networks, because of a shortage of local carers. It has released short films challenging myths about fostering teenagers, and has opened a Fostering Hub Home where young people can get to know foster carers before moving in with them long term.

Wakefield pays its own carers a weekly allowance for each child, from £177 for a child up to two to £267 for a young person of 16 or over, plus a weekly skill-based payment of £53 to £477 depending on the carer's level. The council also pays a £500 welcome bonus after three months with a child, a further £500 after the first 12 months, and from April 2026 a £500 yearly loyalty payment for carers who offer placements for 48 weeks or more. Our Wakefield allowance page has the full figures.

Agencies set their own fees and support, so it is worth speaking to Fostering Wakefield and two or three of the agencies below, and asking each about training, out-of-hours help and what they pay, before you decide.
